title: Deliver an unfamiliar report

outcomes.can: Predict what a join does to a total.
Deliver a complete report from an unfamiliar request without help.

intro: This last module is an assessment. The request is new and uses a table the lessons have not reported on. It needs ideas from the whole course: joins, grouping, a filter on groups, labels, and counts that are safe from fan-out. Reading a finished solution can explain an approach, but it does not show that you can solve the task yourself. Use the contract in the prompt to decide when your work is complete.

steps.title: Read the request before writing
steps.text: Name the rows of the report first. Then list its numbers and note which table each comes from. Two numbers that come from two different tables, each with many rows per product, cannot be added up in one joined query, because each table's rows would repeat the other's. Give each its own step. Before you trust the result, test one row by hand with a plain query on a single table.

steps.title: Predict the result
steps.text: Product 6 has 2 reviews and 11 order items. The query joins both tables to the product. Predict joined_rows.

steps.title: Trace the result
steps.text: Each of the 2 reviews is paired with each of the 11 items, so the join has 22 rows. A count of reviews over those rows would say 22, and a sum of quantities would be doubled. The two DISTINCT counts recover the true numbers for counting, but a sum has no such repair, so the units must be added up before the reviews are joined.

steps.title: Report on reviewed products
steps.text: Work from the contract in the prompt. There are no steps to follow. Save to check the complete submission. Any correct query is accepted.

choices.feedback: The join pairs every review with every item. The two numbers multiply.
2 reviews times 11 order items gives 22 joined rows.
Each of the 11 items appears once for each of the 2 reviews.

review.evidence: Open a fresh starter on a later visit, with the earlier answer closed. A first unaided pass on every case is later evidence of the skill. A hinted pass stays recorded as assisted.

drillGap: No practice drill covers a combined report. This assessment is the evidence for the module.
